title: Spire Mod Manager (Beta)
description:
Spire Mod Manager replaces the game's Modding page with one made for long mod lists: categories, filters, profiles, a load order view, your own notes and tags, and a quick relaunch. The game's own list stays one click away.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]The public-beta branch, game version v0.111.0 or newer, for now.[/b] On the stable branch the game won't load it. To switch: right-click Slay the Spire 2 in your Steam library, then Properties, Betas, public-beta.
[*]No other mods needed.
[*]It doesn't change gameplay, so the people you play multiplayer with don't need it.
[/list]

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Main menu button.[/b] "Mod Profile: Default (12 mods)" in the lower-left corner names your active profile and opens the page. Right-click it to move it or to relaunch the game. A dot shows when a relaunch is pending.
[*][b]Quick with long lists.[/b] Timed with about 250 mods: searching and switching between views take a fraction of a second.
[*][b]Categories.[/b] Sort mods into your own collapsible categories, from a button on each row or the mod's right-click menu. Rename, move or delete a category from its header.
[*][b]Filters.[/b] Show All, Enabled, Disabled or Changed mods. Changed shows the mods changed since the game started. Filters work together with the search, and Enable all and Disable all act on the mods shown.
[*][b]Profiles.[/b] Save which mods are on and switch between sets. When the list differs from the saved profile, it shows "Unsaved" with Save, Save as new and Discard. Hover "Unsaved" to see exactly what changed, or click it for the full list. Switching to another profile keeps the unsaved changes with the one you left. A mod you subscribe to joins the active profile, enabled.
[*][b]Load Order view.[/b] Drag mods into order, one or several at a time, or use Top, Up, Down and Bottom. Hover or drag a mod to see lines to the mods it needs and the mods that need it: green where the order works, red where it doesn't. If a mod sits above a mod it needs, a warning offers Fix now. Auto sort puts libraries first, then gameplay mods, then visual mods, and keeps your order within each group.
[*][b]Warnings that name the mods.[/b] A banner above the list says when enabled mods need a mod that is disabled or not installed. Enable needed mods turns on the ones you have, and Show steps through the mods. Hover a warning, here or in Load Order, to list the mods it's about.
[*][b]Your notes on each mod.[/b] Give a mod an alias, notes and your own tags. Edit them in the info panel or from the mod's right-click menu. Your tags are suggested as you type. Automatic tags are added for you: New, Local, Library, Gameplay and Cosmetic.
[*][b]Search.[/b] Searches names, aliases, notes, tags, authors, categories and Workshop tags. Type #tag to match a tag and @author to match an author. Click a tag or an author to search for it, or Shift-click to add it to the search or take it out. Ctrl+F jumps to the search box.
[*][b]Select several mods.[/b] Ctrl-click, Shift-click or Ctrl+A. Then right-click to set their category, tags or notes together, or turn them all on or off.
[*][b]Changes, undo and redo.[/b] The bar at the bottom counts what changed since the game started. Click it for the full list. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo. Revert all puts things back the way they were when you opened the page.
[*][b]Relaunch Game.[/b] Restarts the game in place, in the same window mode, so your changes apply without going back through Steam. It checks first for mods that won't load (a mod they need is off or missing) and offers to turn on what they need or turn them off.
[*][b]Workshop details in the info panel.[/b] Published and updated dates, size, subscribers, Workshop tags, supported branches and a link to the mod's change notes. Problems, such as a missing dependency, show first in red.
[*][b]Vanilla List.[/b] The game's own Modding page, unchanged, one click away.
[/list]

[h2]Better Mod Menu[/h2]
Both mods can be on at the same time, and they're tested together.
[list]
[*]The first time it runs, Spire Mod Manager copies Better Mod Menu's groups, aliases, notes and profiles. Better Mod Menu's own file is never changed.
[*]Better Mod Menu's page takes the place of the game's list: the Vanilla List button opens it.
[*]The two keep separate profiles. Changes here also change Better Mod Menu's current profile, and switching its profile shows up here as unsaved changes. Our profiles never turn Better Mod Menu on or off.
[*]With both on, a yellow warning above the list says more than one mod manager is enabled. Hover it to see which. Both mods change the same page. If you're happy running both, Dismiss hides the warning until one of them is disabled and enabled again. If something looks wrong, try again with one of them off, and tell me what happened.
[*]Better Mod Menu 1.1.1 has some errors of its own on the beta branch, with or without this mod.
[/list]

[h2]Your data[/h2]
Categories, aliases, notes, tags and profiles are saved in one file per Steam account. On Windows:
[code]%APPDATA%\SlayTheSpire2\steam\(your Steam ID)\mod_data\SpireModManager\manager.json[/code]
The first save of each session makes a backup in the backups folder next to it. The last 10 are kept. If the file can't be read, it's kept aside under a new name and the newest backup that reads loads instead (with none, it starts fresh); a notice says which. If the file can't be moved aside, it stays as it is and that session's changes aren't saved.
This file is not in Steam Cloud, so it doesn't follow you to another PC or a Steam Deck.
Which mods are on, and their load order, stay where the game keeps them. Spire Mod Manager changes the same list as the game's own Modding page.

[h2]Uninstalling[/h2]
Unsubscribe here. The game's own Modding page keeps working: your mods stay on or off as you last set them, in the same load order. The data folder above stays behind. Delete it if you want everything gone.

[h2]Controls[/h2]
Mouse and keyboard only for now. Controller support may come later.

[h2]Bugs and ideas[/h2]
Post in the comments below. It helps to include:
[list]
[*]your game version and branch;
[*]what you did, and what happened;
[*]your log file, %APPDATA%\SlayTheSpire2\logs\godot.log (it can show your Windows user name in file paths).
[/list]
Or open an issue on GitHub: [url=https://github.com/jciurc/spire-mod-manager/issues]github.com/jciurc/spire-mod-manager[/url]. The source code is there too, under the MIT license, and pull requests are welcome.

[h2]Known limits[/h2]
[list]
[*]Public-beta branch only, for now. That changes once v0.111.0 or newer reaches the stable branch.
[*]Slay the Spire 2 is in Early Access. A game update can break parts of this mod until a fix is out. If it breaks the page itself, you get the game's own Modding page, with a line saying Spire Mod Manager needs an update.
[*]Other mod managers change the same page. Only Better Mod Menu has been tested alongside it, so use one manager at a time otherwise.
[*]Relaunch Game is tested on Windows only. macOS, Linux and Steam Deck are untested.
[*]Your data stays on this PC (see Your data).
[*]Its own text is English only for now. Dates and numbers follow the game's language. With the game in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Russian or Polish, it uses the game's font for that language, so mod names, tags and notes written in it show properly.
[/list]
changeNote: 0.1.0: first release. Beta branch only for now (public-beta, game v0.111.0 or newer).
